temperature_range: 300°C for buffer layer growth, 420°C for epilayer growth
summary: InSb films were grown on GaAs substrates using atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) to reduce defects caused by lattice mismatch. The study focused on the growth of high-quality InSb layers and diodes, with a particular emphasis on electron mobility and leakage current characteristics. The results showed that the buffer layer significantly reduced defect density, leading to improved electron mobility, although leakage currents remained high.
evidence: InSb epilayers on the GaAs substrates were grown at a rate of 1 pm/h at a substrate temperature of 420°C after a 300 8, buffer layer of InSb was grown by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) at a growth rate of 0.1 pm/h at 300°C. The first 5 pm layer was grown undoped at a growth rate of 1 pm/h and at a substrate temperature of 420°C. The top 0.6 pm Be-doped P-type layer was grown at a lower substrate temperature, 340°C and with a slower growth rate, 0.5 pm/h, to reduce the migration of Be.
